questions.title: Q2 · Power & data-center capacity (CIFR, CORZ, NBIS)
questions.owner_question: Power is extremely scarce in an AI bull case, CIFR and CORZ have contracted buyers, and 'even if someone goes bankrupt, others will take their place'. Double down on CIFR and CORZ, and own or add to NBIS?
questions.answer_headline: Don't double down (6-0). Hold CORZ and NBIS through their prints; hold CIFR with no adds.
questions.consensus: Energized MW really is scarce, but the toll protects the building, not the leveraged equity. These are single-tenant leases funded 70-100% with debt. In Chapter 11 a tenant can reject leases, and landlord claims are capped at about a year of rent and unsecured. Re-leasing takes 6-18 months while debt payments continue. Upside needs NEW leases, which Texas politics and Microsoft's neocloud pullback now threaten. 'Under $5B' ignores debt: CIFR's and CORZ's enterprise values are about $7.4B and $7.3B. Keep the sleeve near 10% of the book with no adds.

verdicts.rationale: Best operating landlord (485/590 MW billing, $1B Morgan Stanley facility), but a CoreWeave credit proxy (84% of sales). No adds before CoreWeave reports Nov 10.
Least-levered neocloud with pricing power (~20% price hikes). Hold through the Nov 12 print; halve it if Microsoft volumes aren't confirmed.

Best tenants (AWS plus a Google-backstopped Fluidstack lease) but the thinnest equity cushion and nearly all in Texas. Votes split 3-3 on halving it, so hold with no adds; first to be cut if a kill trigger fires.

rejected.reason: The equity is a call option on $51.6B of debt yielding >15%.
Texas and/or CoreWeave concentration, Microsoft delays, serial dilution.
High debt, mostly pipeline value, or tenant-friendly lease terms.

notes: Designated swap target: TLN (nuclear power sold to AWS through 2042; 13.4x, PEG 0.33) if CORZ or CIFR kill triggers fire.

questions.title: Q3 · Robotics (FANUY, YASKY, HSYDF)
questions.owner_question: VC money and industry stalwarts are all in on physical AI. Are these Japanese picks-and-shovels the Micron/SK Hynix of robotics? (Follow-up: I'm still big on robotics. Does any stock make the cut?)
questions.answer_headline: Exit all three; their capital moves to FORM, SITM and CRDO. No pure-play robotics stock makes the cut yet (6-0), and v50 redirected the NVDA robot-brain slot to CRDO (3-3 tie).
questions.consensus: The Micron analogy fails. Memory had 3 suppliers, China blocked from HBM, and multi-year fab lead times. Robot parts have the opposite: Leaderdrive, Inovance, Schaeffler, Nidec and Timken are flooding reducers and servos, and capacity can be added in 12-18 months. Robotics VC money today mostly buys compute (Figure: $3.5B for up to 100K Vera Rubin GPUs), which the book already captures through TSM, ASML, LRCX, CRDO, FORM and ONTO. v49 parked $10K in NVDA as the robot brain; on the v50 AI-compute ballot that slot tied 3-3 and went to CRDO, because robot silicon is ~1% of NVIDIA revenue and a $4.5T stock can't move a multi-bagger book. MP stays on the watchlist (70x, a China-policy trade while the rare-earth truce holds). Pure plays come in only on hard evidence.

verdicts.rationale: Best of the three (orders +49%, net cash), but +8% revenue at 25x (PEG 2.4) and no humanoid chokepoint.
Operating profit falling despite record orders; Inovance is attacking its servos.
~70x while strain-wave reducers commoditize. OTC ordinary share: sell with limit orders.

rejected.reason: Watchlist (2 for, 4 against): 70x forward, a China-policy trade with the truce extended. Add if China re-restricts magnets after Jan 10, a humanoid maker contracts 10X magnet output, or it falls to <=45x.
Agility: pre-revenue de-SPAC ($1.8M 2025 revenue). Wait for the ~May 3, 2027 lock-up AND paid Digit 5 deliveries, with 18+ months of cash.
Robotics is immaterial to sales today, or the company is loss-making in price-war hardware.
v50: robot-brain slot redirected to CRDO (3-3). Best-in-class quality, but ~2x upside from $4.5T; fortress candidate for new brokerage cash.

notes: Scale robotics toward 8-10% only as triggers hit: >=1,000 paid humanoids per quarter outside pilots at under 3-year payback; a supplier holding >=35% gross margin through China's price war; Optimus/Figure external deliveries with disclosed pricing; a US-listed supplier designed into 2+ top humanoid makers.
Dissents (v50): Red Team, Valuation and Power would keep NVDA $10-15K; Robotics wants a robot slot re-opened (NVDA or ALGM) once non-Tesla humanoid deliveries pass 10K a year.
